title: A stdlib parallel test runner: the full suite on every core, same verdict as serial pytest
description: Measured by the coordinator on 2026-11-12: the full suite takes 166 s on one core of 10 (84% CPU). In the gen-10 wave 3 run, 32 of 95 agent-minutes went to full-suite runs, about 3 per agent. pytest-xdist is not installed and the harness adds no dependencies.
acceptance_criteria: .harness/bin/fast_tests.py shards the test files under .harness/tests across N worker processes (default min(8, cpu count minus 2), flag -j), each running python3 -m pytest on its files with -q -p no:cacheprovider. Longest files first, using durations from the previous run when present, else file size. Standard library only.

Files that hash or compare the live tree run in a SERIAL phase after the parallel phase, alone. The serial list is declared at the top of the file with one reason per entry; test_rehearsal.py is on it unless T-478 makes it safe, and every other entry must be justified by a measured failure in parallel.

Output: one final line in pytest's own shape ('N passed, M skipped in S s') so goal_mode and agents read it unchanged; on failure, each failing test id and its shard's output tail. Exit 0 only when every shard passes. --serial runs plain pytest over the whole directory as a fallback.

Evidence in the handoff: on the same tree, fast_tests and serial pytest report the same passed and skipped counts; wall-clock for both; 3 consecutive fast runs with no failure; a planted failing test in a throwaway copy makes it exit nonzero and names the test.
Per-file processes expose order-dependent tests. List any test file that fails when run alone. Fix it only with a test-only change; otherwise put it on the serial list with the reason.

Where durations are stored, the file must be untracked by git (check .gitignore); no absolute paths in it. Do not edit claude.md or ORCHESTRATION.md: list the doc change in the handoff. Hand off to verifier.

notes.note: HANDOFF -> verifier: fast_tests.py, commit 482cab6. Replay: python3 -m pytest .harness/tests -q -p no:cacheprovider (serial) versus python3 .harness/bin/fast_tests.py; both reported 1225 passed, 4 skipped on 2026-11-12 (serial 166 s; parallel 52 to 65 s on a loaded machine). Design: balanced pytest batches from the previous run's per-test times; test_rehearsal.py runs last with one alone-retry; machine-wide slot cap through portalock; PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE in children. Known: the planted-failure, import-error and timeout cases in T-477 were not run by the producer.

VERDICT done (verifier-speed-runner), replayed in throwaway copies, not taken from the handoff.
1. Equivalence: on a copy of the tree, serial pytest and fast_tests report the same totals (1236 tests in the working-tree copy, 1173 in a HEAD-archive copy) and the same failing set, except test_rehearsal.py::test_live_tree_untouched..., which fails in long serial runs when other processes leave sandboxes under the OS temp dir and passes alone (twice); fast_tests' alone-retry reports it. The copies carry environment failures (no private trust material), identical under both runners. Slow-file splitting by class/test (durations present) was exercised: totals still match. Live tree: the goal_mode full run passed on iteration 1 (108 s); one later direct run failed only in test_rehearsal.py while another agent was editing test_rehearsal.py and run_rehearsal.py in the live tree, reported as FAILED again alone, exit nonzero.
2. Planted failing test in the last shard: exit 1, test id named. Import error in one test file: exit 1, ModuleNotFoundError shown, counted as 1 error. Hang with the batch timeout lowered in the copy: exit 1, TIMEOUT line names the batch; no stray pytest process left.
3. Three consecutive full runs while a process rewrote a test file non-atomically every 50 ms (3332 edits): all three exit 1, and the only new failures were 13 test_rehearsal.py ids, which hash the live tree and so must fail while it changes; no false pass, no crash, same total of 1173 each time.
4. Mutants of fast_tests.py in the copy: ok=True always (caught by planted failure), verdict from counts ignoring exit code (caught by import error), timeout treated as exit 0 (caught by hang). All three exited 0 where the clean runner exits 1.
5. Stdlib only (ast walk of imports; portalock is the harness wrapper); .harness/logs/test_durations.json is ignored at .gitignore line 64, untracked, and holds no absolute paths. Files run alone: the same failing set as the full serial run in the copy, so no order-dependent file beyond the declared serial entry.
GAPS for the coordinator, none blocking: (a) the handoff lacks the doc-change list T-476 asked for: claude.md and ORCHESTRATION.md do not mention fast_tests.py; add it under Core Local Tools and the verifier test protocol. (b) the handoff lacks the 3-run and planted-failure evidence; supplied above. (c) there is no test file for fast_tests.py itself. (d) on a timeout the partial output is dropped (bytes under Python 3.9), so earlier failing ids in that batch are not listed and the passed total understates; verdict is still nonzero. (e) the final line reads 'N passed, M skipped in S.SSs (files, batches...)', pytest's shape plus a suffix.
